predecessors.name: Crown of Castile
predecessors.text: the Crown of Castile (with Granada and Navarre), whose throne Charles took with his mother Joanna in 1516

predecessors.name: Crown of Aragon
predecessors.text: the Crown of Aragon, which included Naples, Sicily and Sardinia (Charles V page)

ledger.x: 1516: Charles I becomes sole sovereign of the Crowns of Castile and Aragon.

March 1516: the Low Countries and the Franche-Comte come to the new state with Charles, who was already their lord: 'In 1506, Charles inherited all of his father's territories in the Low Countries', with the Free County of Burgundy, ten years before this state exists.
1516: the Crown of Aragon, with Naples, Sicily and Sardinia, passes to Charles.
1524: Charles takes Friesland.
1535: Charles V annexes Milan.
1561: the court settles at Madrid.
1568: the Dutch Revolt begins.
ledger.cp: Dutch rebels (William of Orange and the Sea Beggars)

ledger.x: April 1572: the Sea Beggars take Holland and Zeeland towns.
ledger.cp: Dutch rebels (William of Orange and the Sea Beggars)

ledger.x: January 1579: the rebel cause passes to the Union of Utrecht, 'concluding the Union of Utrecht on 23 January 1579'; the Pacification of Ghent of November 1576 had joined all the provinces but Luxembourg in revolt without moving Cliopatria's shape.
ledger.cp: Dutch rebels (William of Orange and the Sea Beggars)

ledger.x: January 1579: the northern provinces leave.
January 1579: the war continues against the Union of Utrecht: 'concluding the Union of Utrecht on 23 January 1579'.
1580: Philip II becomes King of Portugal and the crowns of Spain and Portugal are united.
26 July 1581: the Union becomes the United Provinces: the Act of Abjuration was proclaimed 'on 26 July 1581', 'a de facto declaration of independence from Spain'.
1582: the war goes on with the United Provinces, whose dossier (dutch-republic) starts in 1582; Habsburg Spain infobox 'Dutch Revolt: 1568-1648'.
1640: Catalonia rises against Philip IV.
1 December 1640: the Iberian Union breaks and Spain emerges from it again.
1642: France takes Roussillon from the Spanish side, as the kingdom-of-france dossier records.
30 January 1648: the Peace of Munster ends the war with the Dutch.
30 January 1648: Spain gives up Zeelandic Flanders, North Brabant and Maastricht to the Dutch Republic in the Peace of Munster.
1652: Barcelona falls and Catalonia returns to Spain.
November 1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees gives Roussillon to France.
November 1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees turns France's hold on Roussillon into a cession (the loss above).
November 1659: Artois and a strip of Flanders and Hainaut go to France.

24 May 1667: the War of Devolution opens in the Spanish Netherlands: 'the French crossed the border on 24 May'; Charleroi had a French governor on 2 June, Tournai, Kortrijk and Oudenaarde fell by the end of July, Lille surrendered on 28 August.
February 1668: France overruns Franche-Comte: Conde 'entered Franche-Comte on 4 February'; Besancon and Salins-les-Bains surrendered on 7 February, Dole on 14 February and Gray on 19 February.
2 May 1668: the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, 'signed by Spain and France on 2 May': 'France withdrew from Franche-Comte and the Spanish Netherlands' except eleven towns.
2 May 1668: the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle ends the War of Devolution.

2 May 1668: the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle: France kept 'eleven towns and their surrounding areas': Lille, Armentieres, Bergues, Douai, Tournai, Oudenaarde, Kortrijk, Veurne, Binche, Charleroi and Ath.
Spring 1674: France overruns Franche-Comte for the second time.
Early March 1678: France captures Ypres and Ghent.
17 September 1678: the Treaty of Nijmegen with Spain (armistice 19 August 1678) turns the occupation of Franche-Comte into a cession: France 'received the entire Franche-Comte'.
17 September 1678: 'France returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns in the Spanish Netherlands'.
17 September 1678: the Treaty of Nijmegen: France 'received the entire Franche-Comte and the towns of Ypres, Maubeuge, Cateau-Cambresis, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer and Cassel'.

17 September 1678: Spain recovers Charleroi and Ath, both among the eleven towns France kept in 1668: 'France returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns' and the infobox 'Spain regains Ath and Charleroi'.
November 1683: the War of the Reunions opens in Flanders: 'Spain declared war on France on 26 October 1683'; Courtrai surrendered on 6 November, Diksmuide 'surrendered without a fight on 10th'.
3 June 1684: France takes Luxembourg.
15 August 1684: 'Fighting continued elsewhere until the Truce of Ratisbon on 15 August 1684'; the truce guaranteed 20 years of peace between France and the Empire.
June 1694: after Torroella (27 May) 'the French proceeded to take Palamos on 10 June, Gerona on 29 June' and Hostalric.
20 September 1697: the Treaty of Ryswick ends the war: 'France returns Luxembourg and Kortrijk to Spain'; 'Spain regained Luxembourg and other territories from France'.
20 September 1697: the war ends at Ryswick.
November 1700: the Bourbons succeed the Habsburgs.
1705: Catalonia goes over to the Archduke Charles.
1706: Aragon, Valencia and the Balearics are held for the Archduke.
May 1706: the Allies occupy the Spanish Netherlands, which stay Spanish in law.
1707: Imperial troops seize Naples.
March 1707: Milan passes to Austria.
April 1707: Almansa restores Aragon and Valencia.

1713: the Spanish Netherlands, held by the Allies since 1706, are assigned to the Emperor Charles VI by the Treaty of Utrecht (see the loss to habsburg-monarchy below); the Habsburgs accepted at Rastatt on 7 March 1714.
1713: Naples, Sardinia, Milan and the Spanish Netherlands are assigned to the Emperor Charles VI.
13 July 1713: Gibraltar and Menorca go to Britain.
13 July 1713: Sicily goes to Savoy (Spanish-Savoyard treaty of the same day).
June 1715: Catalonia and Majorca are finally subdued.
August 1717: Spain lands on Sardinia.
July 1718: Spain lands on Sicily.
17 February 1720: the Treaty of The Hague returns Sardinia.
17 February 1720: the Treaty of The Hague returns Sicily (to Austria in an exchange: Victor Amadeus 'was forced to exchange Sicily for that of the less important Kingdom of Sardinia').
1783: Menorca is Spanish again.
August 1794: the French invade Gipuzkoa: 'Moncey followed the exploit by capturing San Sebastian without resistance on 3 August' (after Hondarribia; Tolosa soon after, undated).
November 1794: after the Battle of the Black Mountain ('From 17 to 20 November') Figueres and its fortress 'fell quickly afterward' with 9,000 prisoners; Roses fell on 4 February 1795.
22 July 1795: 'The Peace of Basel ended the war on 22 July 1795'; Spain gave up the eastern two-thirds of Hispaniola 'in exchange for keeping Gipuzkoa'.
22 July 1795: the Peace of Basel ends the war and the occupation of the Girona front; the page does not say in so many words that Figueres and Roses were returned.
November 1798: Britain takes Menorca again: the British fleet arrived off the island on 7 November (table 7-15 November) and the Spanish governor surrendered Ciudadela on 16 November.

6 June 1801: the Treaty of Badajoz: Portugal agreed 'to cede Olivenza to Spain and to pay an indemnity' after the Spanish attack of 20 May 1801; the infobox: 'Portuguese territory returned, except Olivenza, and border territories'.
1802: the Treaty of Amiens 'called for the return of Menorca to Spain'; Richard Bickerton oversaw the British evacuation.
December 1808: the French hold the centre and the north.
January 1810: the French overrun Andalusia.
January 1810: the unoccupied government moves to Cadiz.
August 1812: Madrid and the centre are freed.
March 1813: Madrid is again the capital.
June 1813: Vitoria frees the rest.
1848: Spain takes the Chafarinas Islands.

17 December 1859: the Spanish campaign begins: the Congress of Deputies voted the war on 22 October 1859 and 'On December 17, hostilities were unleashed by the column commanded by Zabala'; Tetouan fell on 6 February 1860.

26 April 1860: 'the Treaty of Wad-Ras or Peace of Tetouan was signed on 26 April 1860': an indemnity of 20,000,000 duros, Spanish administration of Tetouan until it was paid, the 'retrocession' of Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena (Ifni, spanish-empire's land) and the extension of Ceuta and Melilla.
February 1873: the monarchy gives way to the First Spanish Republic.
29 December 1874: the monarchy returns.
December 1884: Spain declares a protectorate over the Rio de Oro coast.
1887: Spain extends its Sahara colony inland.
February 1899: the African posts pass from the overseas empire to the kingdom.
1900: Rio Muni is drawn into the shape.
27 November 1912: the Spanish protectorate in northern Morocco is set up.
June 1921: the Rif War begins.
1922: the Spanish zone shrinks.
1924: a further retreat in the Spanish zone.
May 1926: the Rif War ends.
May 1926: the lost land is recovered with the end of the Rif War.
14 April 1931: the Spanish protectorate passes to the Second Republic with the rest of the monarchy's land (the loss below).
14 April 1931: the Rio de Oro coast passes to the Second Republic with the rest of the monarchy's land.
14 April 1931: the Sahara interior passes to the Second Republic with the coast.
14 April 1931: the monarchy falls and the Second Republic is proclaimed.
November 1975: the monarchy is restored.

wars.name: Eighty Years' War
wars.outcome: The seven northern provinces left in January 1579 (Union of Utrecht); Spain recognised the United Provinces in the Peace of Westphalia and Munster (30 January 1648).

wars.name: War of the Portuguese Succession
wars.outcome: Philip II succeeded to the Portuguese crown in 1580 and sent the Duke of Alba to Lisbon in June; the two crowns were united until 1640.

wars.name: Franco-Spanish War (1635-1659)
wars.outcome: Treaty of the Pyrenees, 7 November 1659: France gained Artois, Hainaut and Roussillon.

wars.name: Reapers' War
wars.outcome: Revolt suppressed by Spain; Barcelona retaken in 1652; the Treaty of the Pyrenees ceded Roussillon and the northern half of Cerdanya to France.

wars.name: Portuguese Restoration War
wars.outcome: Portugal 'fought successfully for their independence'; Spain 'finally recognized Portugal's sovereignty in the Treaty of Lisbon (1668)'.

wars.name: War of Devolution
wars.outcome: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, 2 May 1668: France withdrew from Franche-Comte and kept eleven towns of the Spanish Netherlands.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War (Spanish part)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Nijmegen with Spain, 17 September 1678: France kept Franche-Comte, Ypres, Maubeuge, Cateau-Cambresis, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer and Cassel and returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns.

wars.name: War of the Reunions
wars.outcome: Truce of Ratisbon, 15 August 1684: 'Spain cedes Luxembourg to France' (infobox); Spain had declared war on 26 October 1683, Courtrai fell on 6 November, Diksmuide on 10 November, Luxembourg on 3 June 1684.

wars.name: Nine Years' War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Rijswijk (1697) restored to Spain the territories France had annexed in this war and the War of the Reunions.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: Philip V kept Spain and the Indies; Utrecht (11 April 1713) and Rastatt (7 March 1714) took Milan, the Netherlands, Naples and Sardinia for Austria, Sicily for Savoy, Gibraltar and Menorca for Britain; Catalonia and Majorca were subdued by June 1715.

wars.name: War of the Quadruple Alliance
wars.outcome: Spain took Sardinia (1717) and Sicily (1718) and gave them up in the Treaty of The Hague of 17 February 1720.

wars.name: War of the Pyrenees
wars.outcome: Peace of Basel, 22 July 1795: Spain gave up the eastern two-thirds of Hispaniola 'in exchange for keeping Gipuzkoa'.

wars.name: War of the Oranges
wars.outcome: Treaty of Badajoz, 6 June 1801: Portugal cedes Olivenza to Spain and pays an indemnity.

wars.name: Peninsular War
wars.outcome: French armies crossed the border in February 1808 and Joseph Bonaparte was crowned on 25 July 1808; Andalusia was invaded on 19 January 1810; Madrid was freed on 14 August 1812; Vitoria on 21 June 1813; the war ended on 17 April 1814.

wars.name: Hispano-Moroccan War (1859-1860)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Wad-Ras, 26 April 1860: indemnity of 20,000,000 duros, Tetouan held until paid, Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena (Ifni) ceded.

wars.name: Spanish-American War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Paris, 10 December 1898: Cuba given up, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines ceded to the United States.

wars.name: Rif War
wars.outcome: The Spanish zone shrank after Annual (July-August 1921) and was recovered by May 1926.

certainty.note: A composite monarchy whose parts (Low Countries, Franche-Comte, the Italian kingdoms, Roussillon) are known by dynastic right and campaign, not survey lines; the Pyrenees frontier is fixed only by the 1659 treaty.
Treaty lines: the Pyrenees 1659, Aix-la-Chapelle 1668, Nijmegen 1678, Rijswijk 1697, Utrecht 1713, The Hague 1720, Paris 1783.

The metropolitan frontier is sharp; the Spanish Sahara interior (from 1887) and the Rif zone are soft until the conventions of 27 June 1900, 1904 and 12 November 1912, and the 1921-1926 front is soft.
